distinguishing_features: Actively nullifies pressure-driven gas flow asymmetry during sintering using recorded telemetry
Applies direct mechanical pressure compensation to counter differential shrinkage stress
Uses existing kiln pressure and airflow data to infer local partial pressure difference across substrate
Prevents warp by equalizing effective pressure boundary conditions on opposing faces
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent differential shrinkage-induced warp in thin ceramic substrates during sintering caused by asymmetric gas flow and pressure gradients
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism uses established Darcy flow principles and standard pneumatic components to implement a feasible, real-time pressure compensation system.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The application of telemetry-driven, active pressure equalization to prevent sintering warp is not an obvious extension of prior monitoring-only or passive symmetry approaches.
